_comment_research_max: Upper bound of the adjustable multiplier slider. The top value (4.91) is the Velocify figure: contacting inside 1 minute converted 391% better than at the 2 minute mark. Bands below it are scaled down from that ceiling. Nothing here is invented above a published number.

basis.under_1_min: You are already at the top of every dataset on this. Nothing to recover.
basis.1_to_5_min: Velocify found conversion falls off sharply after the first minute, so there is a little left on the table even inside five.
basis.5_to_30_min: MIT/Oldroyd measured a 21x drop in qualification odds between 5 and 30 minutes. This is the front edge of that curve.
basis.30_to_60_min: Past 30 minutes you are on the wrong side of the MIT qualification cliff.
basis.same_day: Harvard Business Review found firms answering within an hour were 7x likelier to qualify a lead than those answering in the second hour.
basis.next_day: HBR measured a 42 hour average first response across 2,241 companies. Next-day replies sit in the slow half of that.
basis.whenever: HBR found 23% of companies never responded at all. No fixed process puts you in that group some of the time.

sources.detail: 3.5 million leads analyzed. Contacting inside 1 minute converted 391% better than at the 2 minute mark.
15,000 leads studied. A lead contacted at 5 minutes was 21x likelier to qualify than one contacted at 30.
2,241 US companies audited. Average first response took 42 hours. 23% never responded at all.
